front.title: Command Authority Across Long Delay and Intermittent Contact

abstract.t: An enforcement point that checks agent-originated commands offline can be out of contact with the party that issues authority for anything from about 2.6 seconds to about two weeks, and learns of no revocation in that time. This document profiles the Command Authority Envelope of the operational-technology command authority profile for that case. Two implementations have to agree on how an enforcement point decides, from a signed revocation status and a monotonic counter, that revocation status has gone silent past a declared budget, and on what a grant written in advance, a contingency grant, permits during that silence. The profile adds one grant field and one declared bound, a second revocation latency budget for the grants that field marks. It also states how expiry and maximum age are checked against a declared clock uncertainty, which way an unknown revocation check fails for each action class, and how a human approval signed before a command departs stays bound to one action.
